title: Contextual Eval Journey: retrieval + long-context distillation notes
highlights: Sketch of distillation pipeline for compressing retrieved context
Experiment matrix for prefix-length vs. quality tradeoffs
Open questions about cache invalidation and hallucination when retrieving stale docs
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad to capture readings, decisions, and next-step experiments while exploring retrieval-augmented long-context distillation. Not polished — notes-to-self + TODOs.

Topline takeaways (from papers/blogs read 7/2029):
- Distillation for long-context: promising to compress multi-document retrieved context into a compact latent prefix that the base LM can consume without full token-expansion. Key tradeoff: compression ratio vs. attribution fidelity.
- Retrieval freshness matters more when user prompts rely on recent facts; hallucination rates climb when distillation pipeline doesn't incorporate document timestamps/versions.
- Hybrid approach seems best: keep small explicit window of recent tokens + latent prefix summarizing older docs.

Papers skimmed (quick notes):
- "Latent Prefix Distillation for Retrieval-Heavy Tasks" (arXiv 2029): good ablations on prefix length; they show linear quality drop beyond 512 compressed-dim steps. Their training recipe uses offline distillation with synthetic retrieval noise.
- "Temporal-Aware RAG" (ACL 2028 demo): timestamp embeddings + version gating reduced stale-hallucinations by ~18% on news QA.
- "Prefix Cache: Memory-efficient KV for Long Inputs" (sys workshop): practical caching heuristics and eviction TTLs; inspired some cache-invalidation ideas below.

My quick sketch of a pipeline (very rough):
1) Retrieval (BM25 + dense) returns top-K docs with metadata (ts, source_id, score).
2) Pre-filter: drop docs older than retention threshold unless high relevance score OR linked-to canonical id.
3) Distillation encoder: offline/batched student that compresses top-K into a fixed-length latent prefix vector (or short token sequence) and produces attribution pointers.
4) Runtime runtime: LM consumes [recent explicit tokens] + [latent prefix] as a single context. Retrieval metadata passed to console for traceability.
5) Post-hoc attribution: map tokens in generated output back to pointer probabilities from the distillation step for audit.

Open questions / risks:
- How to keep attributions meaningful if a latent prefix merges many docs? (prob: keep per-doc pointer vectors alongside latent prefix and propagate alignment scores)
- Cache staleness: need TTLs keyed by source_id + content-hash. If doc updates, invalidate derived latent prefixes. But cost: recompute distillation for many customers -> expensive.
- Latent prefixes and RLHF/finetuned models: does compressing context interact badly with instruction-following behaviors? Need a small suite of behavioral probes.
- Privacy/compliance: if latent prefix mixes private doc fragments, how to ensure revocation or right-to-be-forgotten? Must bind prefixes to customer keys and provide deletion propagation.

Experiment matrix (short term):
- Variables: top-K retrieval size {5, 10, 20}, explicit-token-window {256, 512, 1024}, latent-prefix-length {64, 128, 256}, distillation-loss {CE, contrastive}, freshness-filter {on/off}.
- Metrics: answer-EM/F1 on curated QA sets, hallucination rate (manual labeling sample), latency p50/p95, cost-per-query (in GPU-seconds), attribution-precision (how often exported pointer matches human-annotated source).
- Start small: run offline distillation on a 100k doc news+kb corpus, evaluate on 3 microbenchmarks (news QA, procedure-following, multi-hop retrieval).

Immediate TODOs (week):
- [ ] Fork github repo and add a toy trainer for latent prefix (use existing transformer encoder + small MLP to project to token-like sequence). Goal: end-to-end toy demo in 2 weeks.
- [ ] Craft 3 probing prompts to test behavioral regressions (instruction following, refusal, factuality) when prefix is used vs full-context.
- [ ] Talk to infra (Omar) about cost model: how often can we refresh prefixes under expected QPS for beta customers?
- [ ] Write short note for legal/privsec: implications of caching compressed customer data (tag: privacy-flag).

Notes to self / heuristics: 
- When K is small and latent prefix short, prefer contrastive distillation loss to preserve unique IDs.
- Keep a conservative TTL default (7 days) and provide per-customer override.
- Instrument per-request debug: original doc ids + compressed-hash so we can repro and recompute when needed.

Random links and snippets saved: 
- Example ablation table from paper: "prefix-len vs EM drop" -> capture in spreadsheet (link above).
- Slack convo: #applied-ml thread "prefix-distill-approach" (see pinned messages for initial sketches).

Longer-term ideas (wishlist):
- Distillation-as-a-service: incremental recompute pipeline triggered by doc-change events; maintain per-customer index of latent-prefix shards.
- Hierarchical prefixes: micro-prefixes per doc cluster + global context combiner. Might reduce recompute blast radius.
- Integrate Redwood Optimize: surface quantization recommendations for prefix model (size/FP format) to lower cost.

Final quick reflections:
- This direction feels useful for customers trying to scale retrieval without linear token costs. Biggest friction is engineering cost of recompute + attribution fidelity.
- Prioritize a reproducible toy that shows quality parity (or small degradation) with large cost win. That will sell the idea internally.

Bottom-line next meeting agenda (with Omar, Hannah):
- Show toy-training plan + dataset selection (15m)
- Discuss TTL and recompute budget (15m)
- Decide initial evaluation set and labeling plan (15m)

End of scratchpad. Will keep iterating here as experiments run.
